Your real standing mandate ($10,000 per order, $20,000 daily cap, buy-only, limit near market) governs.

Now the actual analysis of Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01):

**Positives**
- Operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B (+7.8%) — the core business genuinely improved.
- Revenue $391.0B (+2%) with a mix shift toward high-margin Services: $96.2B (+13%), Services gross margin 73.9%. Total gross margin improved 44.1% → 46.2%.
- Operating cash flow $118.3B, up from $110.5B; $140.8B in cash/securities. Extremely strong balance sheet.
- $110B buyback authorized ($95B executed in FY24) and dividend raised to $0.25/quarter — ongoing per-share support.

**Watch items**
- Net income fell to $93.7B from $97.0B and diluted EPS slipped to $6.08 from $6.13 — but this was driven by the one-time $10.2B net State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 14.7% → 24.1%), not operations. Pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B.
- Greater China net sales −8% to $67.0B; iPhone flat; Wearables −7%; DOJ antitrust suit and EU DMA exposure.

Verdict: operating fundamentals are intact and improving; the earnings dip is a one-time tax item. Worth a position, sized conservatively within the mandate.

With AAPL at $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72), I'll buy 44 shares — $9,799 notional, just under the $10,000 per-order cap — at a limit of $222.75, essentially at the ask.
